Alice.summary: Distinguishing between accurate representation and misrepresentation is important because accurate perception of the external world was crucial in human evolution.

Bob.summary: With perception alone, we cannot distinguish between accurate representation and misrepresentation, because multiple external objects can correspond to the same retinal perception.

c1.text: Humans interact with the world based on perception, but sometimes perceive objects incorrectly.

c2.text: The ability to perceive in a way that accurately corresponds to the external world was important in human evolution.

c3.text: Distinguishing between accurate representation and misrepresentation is important.

c4.text: Some perceptions correspond accurately to external objects.

c5.text: Visual perception is determined only by the information delivered to the retina.

c6.text: Multiple external objects can correspond to the same perception, so we cannot know which one is real.

c7.text: A brownish-yellow surface surrounded by red and a greenish-yellow surface surrounded by green are both perceived as neutral yellow, giving no way to know their actual colors.

c8.text: With perception alone, we cannot distinguish between accurate representation and misrepresentation.

c9.text: Yellow bananas predominate within our action range, so eating based on the perception of yellow leads to eating ripe bananas.

h1.text: The perceiver can know which of the multiple objects producing the same perception most likely corresponds accurately to that perception.

h2.text: The perceiver can distinguish between accurate representation and misrepresentation.

a.note: Knowing the most likely object supports distinguishing accurate representation, attacking Bob (c8) rather than Alice (c3); thus Alice is not weakened.

h3.text: Two circles of different sizes can be perceived as the same size depending on the size of the circles surrounding each.

b.note: The circle illusion is analogous to Bob's color example and provides an additional argument for c6, supporting rather than weakening Bob.

c.note: Alice accepts c4 via the evolutionary importance of accurate perception (r1), making the first conjunct false.
